es.summary: Inhibidor de la neuraminidasa usado para tratar y prevenir la influenza tipo A y B.
key_points: Debe iniciarse dentro de las 48 h del inicio de los síntomas.
Se administra por vía oral; la formulación de suspensión es útil en pediatría.
Ajuste de dosis en insuficiencia renal moderada a grave.
Los efectos adversos más frecuentes son náuseas y vómitos.
No sustituye la vacunación anual contra la influenza.

mechanism: Bloquea la enzima neuraminidasa viral, impidiendo la liberación de nuevas partículas virales.
Reduce la propagación del virus en el epitelio respiratorio.
indications: Tratamiento de influenza confirmada o sospechada en pacientes ≥ 1 año.
Profilaxis post‑exposición en contactos cercanos sin inmunidad.
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad conocida al oseltamivir o a cualquiera de sus excipientes.
Pacientes con insuficiencia renal grave sin ajuste de dosis.
adverse_effects: Reacción alérgica grave: urticaria, angioedema, anafilaxia (serio).
interactions: Probenecid puede aumentar los niveles plasmáticos de oseltamivir.
La vacuna viva atenuada contra influenza puede reducir su eficacia si se administra simultáneamente.
nursing_care: Verificar diagnóstico de influenza y tiempo de inicio de síntomas (< 48 h).
Evaluar función renal (creatinina sérica) antes de iniciar terapia.
Administrar con alimentos para minimizar náuseas.
Monitorear signos de deshidratación y registrar ingesta de líquidos.
Retener la dosis si el paciente presenta vómitos persistentes y notificar al médico.
Observar cualquier signo de reacción alérgica y reportar inmediatamente.
patient_teaching: Iniciar el tratamiento lo antes posible, idealmente dentro de las 48 h.
Completar el curso completo aunque los síntomas mejoren.
Tomar el medicamento con alimentos o leche para reducir molestias gastrointestinales.
Informar al profesional de salud si aparecen erupciones cutáneas, dificultad para respirar o vómitos intensos.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Hidratación adecuada: ingesta de líquidos ≥ 2 L/día en 24 h.
Peso estable: variación < 0.5 kg en 24 h.

interventions.action: Evaluar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Detectar déficit de volumen temprano y guiar la reposición.

interventions.action: Ofrecer líquidos claros y/o solución de rehidratación oral cada 2 h.
Monitorear signos vitales (PA, FC, temperatura) y mucosas cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Identificar cambios hemodinámicos relacionados con la pérdida de líquidos.

interventions.action: Registrar peso diario y comparar con peso basal.
interventions.rationale: Detectar pérdida de peso súbita como indicador de déficit de volumen.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente y familia sobre la importancia de la ingesta regular de líquidos.
interventions.rationale: Promover la adherencia al plan de hidratación.

en.summary: Neuraminidase inhibitor used to treat and prevent influenza type A and B.
key_points: Must be started within 48 h of symptom onset.
Administered orally; suspension formulation useful in pediatrics.
Dose adjustment in moderate to severe renal impairment.
Most common adverse effects are nausea and vomiting.
Does not replace annual influenza vaccination.

mechanism: Blocks viral neuraminidase enzyme, preventing release of new viral particles.
Reduces viral spread in the respiratory epithelium.
indications: Treatment of confirmed or suspected influenza in patients ≥ 1 year.
Post‑exposure prophylaxis in close contacts without immunity.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to oseltamivir or any excipient.
Patients with severe renal impairment without dose adjustment.
adverse_effects: Severe allergic reaction: urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis (serious).
interactions: Probenecid may increase plasma levels of oseltamivir.
Live attenuated influenza vaccine may reduce its efficacy if administered simultaneously.
nursing_care: Verify influenza diagnosis and symptom onset time (< 48 h).
Assess renal function (serum creatinine) before starting therapy.
Administer with food to minimize nausea.
Monitor for dehydration signs and record fluid intake.
Withhold dose if patient has persistent vomiting and notify the physician.
Observe for any signs of allergic reaction and report immediately.
patient_teaching: Start treatment as soon as possible, ideally within 48 h.
Complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
Take medication with food or milk to reduce gastrointestinal discomfort.
Inform healthcare provider if skin rashes, breathing difficulty, or severe vomiting occur.

outcomes: Adequate hydration: fluid intake ≥ 2 L/day within 24 h.
Stable weight: variation < 0.5 kg within 24 h.

interventions.action: Assess fluid intake and output every 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Detect early fluid deficit and guide replacement.

interventions.action: Offer clear fluids and/or oral rehydration solution every 2 h.
Monitor vital signs (BP, HR, temperature) and mucous membranes each shift.
interventions.rationale: Identify hemodynamic changes related to fluid loss.

interventions.action: Record daily weight and compare to baseline weight.
interventions.rationale: Detect sudden weight loss as an indicator of fluid deficit.

interventions.action: Educate patient and family on the importance of regular fluid intake.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Antibiotic, Antiviral/Anti–COVID-19, and Antifungal Drugs
Pharmacology for Nurses: Feminizing Hormonal Therapy

key_points.0.quote: Clients using the episodic method must be instructed to begin taking their therapy within 24 hours of symptom onset for the medication to be effective.

sections.mechanism.0.quote: Neuraminidase inhibitors work by inhibiting the enzyme neuraminidase, which is used to cleave mature copies of the virus from an infected cell to allow it to go infect other cells.

sections.contraindications.0.quote: A contraindication to any antiviral drug is known hypersensitivity.

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Most oral antibiotics can cause gastrointestinal discomfort, including nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: Allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, are possible with penicillins.

sections.nursing_care.5.quote: The client taking an antiviral should: Alert their health care provider about any signs of allergic reactions, including throat swelling, severe itching, rash, or chest tightness.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: For episodic use, begin taking the antiviral as soon as possible (within 24 hours of symptom onset) to reduce symptom duration.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Take the entire course of antibiotics, even if they begin to feel better.
